output.summary: A root vegetable native to Eurasia, wild parsnip is related to carrot but is paler and more strongly flavoured. Its root and the part just above it are eaten cooked in stews and soups, while other plant parts are toxic. Cultivated since ancient times, it served as a staple before potatoes were introduced.
output.edibilityNote: The root and adjoining lower stem are eaten cooked; other plant parts are toxic.
